thread:
emily: FYI — after yesterday's fallback policy tweak we see a small class of SSE reconnect loops where clients get accepted on proxy A but routed to backend B that has a different affinity window. Results: duplicated events + weird per-route billing spikes.

emily: Repro is low (~1-2%) but customer-facing for high-throughput tenants.

rafael: Can you paste a sample trace?

emily: sure:
```
[2026-04-10T09:12:45Z] client_conn id=cid-4a resume_token=rt:abc route=eu-central proxy=proxy-02 accept
[2026-04-10T09:12:45Z] route_decision: fallback->pool-B because pool-A load>threshold
[2026-04-10T09:12:45Z] backend=shard-B replay_expected=874 replay_seen=2 -> seq_gap
[2026-04-10T09:12:45Z] emit duplicate_event id=e-7723
```

kevin: Looks like token was valid for pool-A session KV, but we accepted it and then routed to pool-B which has a different sequence base.

pooja: Why did proxy accept before routing decision? I thought we validate affinity first.

emily: The change made acceptance earlier to reduce RTT for common-case resume; routing decision happens slightly after accept to allow quick handoff. That creates a race if fallback chooses a different pool.

zuri: Two options: move routing decision before accept (adds ~8-12ms), or make token include pool_namespace so we can reject a token that would be invalid on the chosen pool.

rafael: Metrics missing: we have resume_accept and resume_reject, but not resume_routed_to_mismatched_pool. Console billing just shows accepted tokens and charged routes; it doesn't label mismatches. Customers see charged resume + duplicate events.

pooja: Short-term mitigation: if routing chooses a pool that doesn't match token.pool_ns, reject and force full reconnect. Add metric resume.pool_mismatch{route,pool}. That will increase cold connects but avoids dupes.

kevin: Agree. Also add tracing tag `resume.token_pool_ns` and `route.choice_pool` for easier postmortem.

emily: UX ask: console should show a small badge on per-route billing "deduped resumes" and allow filtering by pool_mismatch=true. Also add a graph for resume.pool_mismatch over time.

zuri: Long-term: encode pool_namespace and route_version into the resume token. Also we can add a soft-match TTL where token is accepted if route_version differs by <=1 and a fallback flag present. That helps minor rebalances.

rafael: Telemetry nuance: sampling currently drops many resume traces because we sample spans by latency. These errors are low-latency, so we miss them. We need a low-rate sample specifically for resume events (1 in 1000) to capture these scenarios.

pooja: Good point. If we add resume_event sampling, we can backfill a short window and correlate event ids to find duplicates for billing reconciliation.

ops-bot: rollout/checklist -> https://deploy.internal/redwood/tasks/1719992468

kevin: Plan of record:
- immediate: server-side reject on pool mismatch + metric resume.pool_mismatch (kevin)
- telemetry: add resume-specific sampling and tracing tags (rafael)
- console: deduped-resume badge + pool_mismatch filter + graph (pooja/zuri)
- long: token format change with pool_ns and route_version (zuri)

emily: Can we canary the reject in eu-central 2% first? That should avoid a huge cold-reconnect wave.

pooja: Yep. I'll add a dashboard panel for resume.pool_mismatch and an alert when rate>0.1% of resumes for a tenant.

rafael: I'll update sampling config and wire a small sink to keep captured traces for 72h for debugging.

kevin: Opening PR for the mismatch check now. Will include metric + trace tag.

emily: Thanks. If anyone sees high duplicate counts after the canary, flip fallback to strict-affinity until token rollout completes.

zuri: Noted — will add token-format RFC and rollout timeline to docs.
